example.md.overview.shop.back-office.pay.name: Charge once
example.md.overview.shop.back-office.pay.body: Checkout retries the same request. The order service treats a repeated checkout key as the order it already created, so a retry never charges twice.

example.yaml.Parts.actor.name: actor
example.yaml.Parts.actor.description: Someone outside the system who uses it. Drawn wherever they meet it.

example.yaml.Parts.external.name: external
example.yaml.Parts.external.description: A system nobody here runs. The shop meets it only at its edge.

example.yaml.Parts.page.name: page
example.yaml.Parts.page.description: A screen a customer uses. It shows something and asks for something, over HTTP.

example.yaml.Parts.service.name: service
example.yaml.Parts.service.description: Runs on its own, owns its data and speaks to others only through its ports. Every service names the team that runs it: check reports one that does not.

example.yaml.Parts.store.name: store
example.yaml.Parts.store.description: Keeps many records of one type, drawn as a table on its card. Records are values, never blocks.

example.yaml.Records.ledger.name: Ledger
example.yaml.Records.ledger.description: A store of orders: many records of one type, drawn as a table on its card.

example.yaml.Records.line.name: Line
example.yaml.Records.line.description: One product on an order, and how many.

example.yaml.Records.order.name: Order
example.yaml.Records.order.description: A customer's request, and the lines on it.

example.yaml.Records.order.1.name: place
example.yaml.Records.order.1.description: Takes a customer's lines and gives back the order they make.

example.yaml.Records.order.order-states.name: Order states
example.yaml.Records.order.order-states.description: A state machine, the Order record's lifecycle, ranked by where its transitions point. Each transition is named by the event that fires it.

example.yaml.Records.payment.name: Payment
example.yaml.Records.payment.description: A charge taken against an order.

example.yaml.overview.name: Overview
example.yaml.overview.description: The shop in its world: who uses it and what it leans on. Open Shop to go inside; every diagram here is one side of it.

example.yaml.overview.1.name: One shop, seen from every side: open Shop for its parts, and a part for its own diagram. Every part is a usage of a definition in Parts or Records.

example.yaml.overview.shop.name: Shop
example.yaml.overview.shop.description: The shop itself, one region a side: what customers reach, what runs behind it, the records it keeps, and how it runs.

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.o.name: Orders
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.o.description: Keeps every order and tells the rest of the shop when one is placed.

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.o.name: Runbook
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.o.body:
# When orders stop flowing

Check the **relay** first. See the [outbox pattern](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html).

| signal | threshold | page |
|---|---|---|
| outbox rows | 10 000 | yes |
| relay lag | 60 s | no |

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.o.name: Release notes
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.o.body: v2 of the orders API: the checkout key is required.

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.name: Payments
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.description: Takes money for an order, once, and says whether it was taken. Open it for how a charge is retried.

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.name: A retried checkout repeats the same key, so a retry never charges twice.
Incident summary
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.body: Checkout was slow for twenty minutes while the card processor timed out. The breaker opened, the fallback queued charges, and every queued charge was taken once the processor came back.

example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.name: Payment retry
example.yaml.overview.shop.back-office.p.description: A flowchart, one of Payments' behaviours. It starts and ends at its marks; a decision's lines say where each answer goes.

example.yaml.overview.shop.customer-faci.name: Storefront
example.yaml.overview.shop.customer-faci.description: An internal diagram: what the storefront is made of. Its pages meet through typed ports; its own ports sit on its walls.

example.yaml.overview.shop.data.1-model.name: Model
example.yaml.overview.shop.data.1-model.description: The records as classes — fields, then behaviours — joined by the associations stored between them, each end saying how many and in what role. Order status is a type, so it draws no card of its own.

example.yaml.overview.shop.data.2-schema.name: Schema
example.yaml.overview.shop.data.2-schema.description: The records as an entity relationship diagram — columns and keys — the same associations drawn as crow's feet.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.1.name: Checkout saga
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.1.description: A sequence: who talks to whom, in what order. Each lifeline is a reference to the part it stands for, so it is the same Gateway, Storefront and Payments the shop is made of.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.name: Fulfilment
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.description: A swimlane: who does what, in which phase. Each lane is a reference to the service that does the work.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.name: Pick items
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.body: Stock is taken off the shelf.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.name: Book carrier
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.2.body: Shipping books a pickup in the carrier's terms.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.3.name: Deployment
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.3.description: Where the shop runs. Groups nest, each a dashed box round its members with a note tied beside it; a grid lays environments under their headers.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.4.name: Estate
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.4.description: A treemap: where the weight is. Each tile is as large as the service it stands for holds, gathered by the shop's regions.

example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.5.name: Dashboard
example.yaml.overview.shop.how-it-runs.5.description: What the shop looks like from the operations floor: a picture card, drawn from its source.
